Phoenix Empire (F38 / F97)

Survey region (English ranking table): Bulwar.

At a glance: Rebuild the fallen Sun Elf empire, then race against the clock to plant the Phoenix banner at both ends of Halann.

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 98/100 | Autocracy 91/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 66/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; theme intensity 54/100) | Pluralism 36/100. v2.1 values: Neutral (49/100), with a stable trajectory. The score is not reduced simply for conquest, monarchy, or Sun Elf identity. Restoring canals, farmland, cities, and trade routes provides clear public benefit; the missions accept multiple Bulwari cultures and preserve some local administration. But the mission text explicitly advocates eliminating heresy, displacing other faiths in Haless, and potentially burning settlements that resist. Those recognized are subjects loyal to the emperor and Surael, not communities with equal self-determination; this leaves the overall assessment in a dark-leaning Neutral range.

Story: Very high | Mission tree: Very long (49 Phoenix Empire-specific mission definitions; predecessor missions are counted separately) | Mission-tree update: Use the current local files; supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: Medium-high (formation requirements, timed missions, and overextension) | Early pressure: Depends on the predecessor; high after formation | Expansion: Extremely high.

You Do Not Start as an Empire

The current English and Chinese country localisations both display F38 and F97 as Phoenix Empire. They are distinct Tags: F97 is the western-capital variant produced by the same restoration decision when the capital is in a particular location, and both Tags use the same campaign mission tree. Neither represents an intact empire available at the 1444 start. You begin as a Sun Elf country, meet the requirements, and unify Bulwar before placing the ancient imperial name on your state again.

The offline English Wiki calls the first Phoenix Empire “Sarnagir Esralm”: Jaher established it after the Sun Elf landing, conquered Bulwar, and then advanced east into Haless. The Wiki's main page marks Jexis's assassination in 1162 as the empire's end. A separate, more detailed account of the First Cinder War records the governors fighting until 1169; the Kalib Assembly failed to agree on a common emperor in 1170, declared the empire over, and reorganized the governorships as kingdoms. The first account emphasizes the emperor's death and ensuing collapse; the second details the political settlement. They should not be combined into the unqualified claim that “everything collapsed in 1162.” The Mod's country history also preserves the old Jaher and Jexis setting, but its accession dates do not fully match the Wiki. Nor should the territory a player may later reconquer be treated as settled 1444 history. To modern Sun Elf states, “Phoenix” is both an inheritance and a competing claim to legitimacy.

Which Country Can Become the Phoenix?

The formation decision is not exclusive to any one predecessor. Its core requirements include a Sun Elf country and ruler culture, Bulwari Sun Worship, and at least 100 provinces owned in the Bulwar superregion or held there by non-sovereign subjects; the country must also be at peace and meet the independence conditions when the decision is taken. This is not an automatic upgrade for Birzartanšes, nor will every Sun Elf start form the empire at the same pace. A country that has played as Birzartanšes (F21) may also retain that country's unique mission eligibility, so this article counts F21's opening campaign separately from the Phoenix Empire's 49 new missions.

The decision branches on the capital's location at the moment of formation: a capital in the West Cannor superregion produces F97; otherwise it produces F38. Both receive the Phoenix Empire mission set and can use the same palace decisions. The darker flag and the country-file name “Bastard Empire” do not make F97 a separate evil route. The mission tree explicitly excludes countries that have previously been F52; inheritance of any other predecessor content depends on the in-game mission eligibility conditions.

After Restoration, the Empire Still Has to Be Built

Formation is a starting gun, not a finale. The missions first consolidate Bulwar and restore the Bulwar City Canal and the Golden Highway running east–west, bringing the old empire's transport, commerce, and monumental works back into operation. Palace construction is a separate project requiring money, administrative resources, and development in the capital. The country is not only about expanding its army: river-valley farmland, revived cities, goods along the trade routes, and scholars all belong to the restoration story.

The missions then reach west across the Divenhal Sea, Cannor, and East Cannor, and east into Rahen, the City of Stone, and Haless beyond the Phoenix's Sun. The project seeks to reproduce—and even surpass—the domains of Jaher and Jexis. Its text links restored roads, frontline protectorates, conquest, and the faith of Surael: trade routes are military roads, and military roads become channels for spreading the faith. The palace, Phoenix Crown, and intercontinental commerce give an immense territory an imperial center.

The feature that most distinguishes this from ordinary world conquest is time pressure. Formation starts mission timers. Completing several expansion objectives within a window of about 20 years adds to the timed-progress tally; “Wear the Phoenix Crown” requires at least 10 timely completions, a ruler with high abilities, and sufficient crownland. Not all 49 missions are timed, and formation does not trigger a disaster that inevitably causes failure. But it compresses war order, truces, overextension, and administrative development into a demanding schedule. An older player campaign described overextension as the empire's main enemy after formation; that is a personal account from 2023, not a guarantee of current balance.

How Do You Govern an Empire This Large?

The formation effect accepts multiple Bulwari cultures and can integrate eligible regional subjects. The Phoenix missions also allow newly conquered areas to retain their old administration for a time while answering to the emperor and gradually entering the central system. With the relevant DLC, the Phoenix Estate mechanic offers choices among taxes, manpower, and local autonomy, sharing a 20-year cooldown. This is a tool for governing a vast realm, not an egalitarian federation: local administration is retained so the empire can keep conquering, taxing, and mobilizing.

The imperial narrative includes real public works and some acceptance of cultural diversity, alongside pronounced religious exclusion. Bulwari heresy is to be eliminated; other beliefs and religions in Haless are described as needing to give way to Surael. One mission even presents burning resistant settlements and forests as possible methods. It is wrong to condemn the country automatically for being a Sun Elf conquest empire, but equally wrong to call forced conversion simply “bringing the light.” The personality card therefore rates it dark-leaning Neutral: the empire improves cities and trade routes and opposes some forms of enslavement, yet subordinates others' autonomy to religious uniformity and elite imperial order. The assessment concerns the policy direction of the mission route, not a claim that every player enacts every narrative proposal.

Who Is It For?

If you enjoy forming a vast empire from a local kingdom, restoring the old world's roads and palaces while fighting wars across continents, and planning a route around ten timed objectives, the Phoenix Empire is a distinctive long campaign. If you prefer a peaceful small country, fewer wars, or do not want to manage truces and overextension across a huge map, it will probably wear you down. F38 and F97 share one personality card. If you want to play through Birzartanšes's own trials, artillery, and 25-year plan, start with its country entry.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Phoenix Empire (F38) — Phoenix Empire Ideas

Set ID: F38_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        OR = {
            tag = F38
            tag = F97
        }
    }

Phoenix Empire Traditions

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Core-creation cost: -10% (core_creation; raw value -0.1).

1. Mantle of the Conqueror

"The conqueror stood at the world far edge and stared across the sunlit sea, And felt aught but crushing darkness, No thrill of victory. His blood sang for conquest but the world had struck him lame, And he wept great tears of fire and in thundering voice proclaimed. "I have reached my zenith, the highest I shall mark, For there are no more worlds to conquer, my soul is torn apart." He turned to face his empire, resigned to his fate, Jaher's time had passed, his death he did await. Till one takes up the mantle. The Phoenix Crown awaits." -from the Litany of Jaher by Sarada Razumir

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

2. The Order of the Light of Truth

The Sun Elves have long been styled the Chosen of Surael, destined to pave the way for his glorious return. Yet even as the Empire rose from the ashes of Jexis' reign there was a significant minority within its borders who refused to follow the true faith, not to mention those outside the Empire who still clung to dead gods. To combat this the priests of Surael formed The Order of the Light of Truth to spread the teachings of the Sun Temple to the farthest corners of the world, a task they proved apt in achieving.

  • Missionary strength: +3% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.03).

3. The Empire of Palaces and Temples

The Phoenix Empire is one of soaring temples and palaces that reach towards the heavens, from the Palace of Eternal Fire to the Dawn temple its lands are filled with wonders undreamed, draped in marble and gold. It is not uncommon for the Elvish nobility to have sprawling estates larger than most towns as they add grander and grander edifices as the centuries wear on. With its resurgence the new Emperors undertook great projects to craft edifices to surpass anything found in the kingdoms of man and cement the glory of a new age of Elven leadership and peace.

  • Development cost: -5% (development_cost; raw value -0.05).

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

4. From Ashes, the Phoenix Legion rises

In years past Jaher and Jexis lead the finest armies that the world has ever seen in their conquests. Legends of endless ranks of Legionaries clad in glittering golden armour and armed with shining silver blades are told across all of Cannor. Since the fall of Jexis the proud warrior traditions of the Phoenix Legions has faded into history and no more golden warriors march across Sarhal for the glory of the Sun Elf people.

Now that our great Empire has been reformed from the ashes, so too must the Legions march. For too long have those blades of legend been left to rust and dull under the weight of years. Once more the Phoenix Legions shall rise and once more the enemies of the Sun Elves shall tremble at their passing.

  • Infantry combat ability: +20% (infantry_power; raw value 0.2).

5. The Offices of Trade

Trade is one of the most vital practices in the Empire, much of the Elves' vast wealth is drawn from eastern goods traveling along the Empire's trade routes to be sold in the western lands of Cannor. To facilitate this trade, as well as to give an edge to their own merchant class, the Imperial government set about establishing a series of way stations called The Offices of Trade throughout its vast holdings where their merchants could rest and prepare for long journeys.

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

  • Movement speed: +15% (movement_speed; raw value 0.15).

6. The Gilded Menagerie

In the imperial capital of Bulwar, near to the Imperial Palace, lies a vast and sprawling complex of gold and lapis lazuli. Its official name is the Imperial Academy of Progress but most know it by another name The Gilded Menagerie. It is here that the future governors of the Empire are trained, many a noble house has sent its scions here in order to gain favour and position within the Imperial Bureaucracy. Its darker purpose is the training ground of the Empire's vast network of spies and assassins. It is said that in every court in Cannor, in every gathering of mages the Menagerie has a dozen sets of ears listening to every word and a dozen sharpened knives at every back.

  • Spy network construction: +25% (spy_offence; raw value 0.25).

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

7. United under the Chosen People

The Phoenix Empire and its Sun Elf rulers are masters over vast and diverse lands stretching from horizon to horizon. It is within this Empire more than any other that cultures meet, trade and mingle under the enlightened rule of the chosen. The Sun Elves have accepted their destiny as those who will one day lead the entire world under their glorious rule and accept all the lesser races and accept all into the fold, provided they kneel at the feet of their betters.

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +15% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.15).

Phoenix Empire Ambition

  • Administrative efficiency: +5% (administrative_efficiency; raw value 0.05).
